extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policymakers, media analysts, journalists and civil-society actors interested in public trust and media freedom
extracted.subtask_description: Metadata and descriptive summary for the Edelman Trust Barometer — an annual, cross-country survey dataset measuring public trust in various institutions and media types, used to inform policy, strategy and research. Includes topical keywords, data type and collection method, coverage and provenance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population's trust in media (including search engines, social media, owned media and traditional media)
rubrics_metrics.description: The surveys include questions on the population's trust in media (including search engines, social media, owned media and traditional media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results are analysed by experts and the barometer offers annual global reports based on these survey questions to help inform leadership, strategy, policy and sustained action across institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in government and/or societal leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: The surveys include questions on the population's trust in the government and/or societal leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside other trust metrics to assess public confidence in political authority and leadership; results feed into analysis for governance and policy recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in NGOs
rubrics_metrics.description: The surveys include questions on the population's trust in NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a measure of civil-society credibility and can be compared with trust in other institution types (government, business, media).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The surveys include questions on the population's trust in businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess corporate reputation and public expectations of private-sector actors; analysed to inform business strategy and accountability debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic coverage / sample scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The barometer produces annual global reports based on these multi-country surveys; geographic coverage limits comparability to included countries and years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of data: Quantitative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates numeric survey responses suitable for statistical analysis, trend comparison, and aggregation across samples and countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection method: Survey
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data are self-reported via survey instruments; users should consider survey design, sampling, question wording and timing when interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords / topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords associated with the dataset: COVID-19, Access to information, Freedom of expression, Press freedom, Disinformation, Misinformation, Trust, Governance, Elections, Social media, Legacy media, Transparency, Internet access, Internet universality, Polarization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics indicate thematic areas the dataset is relevant to and can guide researchers on potential analyses (e.g., trust and disinformation, media pluralism, internet access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main thematic categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Main characteristics categories: Media pluralism, Media independance, Digital rights, Socioeconomic context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories frame the dataset's relevance to media development and digital-rights research; note the original spelling 'Media independance' as used on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset/documentation is provided in English; language availability may affect accessibility and applicability across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of provided gender-disaggregated data is a data-limitation flag for analysts interested in sex/gender comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDG focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No SDG focus information provided on the page; users seeking alignment with Sustainable Development Goals will need to determine relevance via topic keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution and license
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of source license: Not apply (N/A). Source — Name of the organization: Edelman; Link to organization: https://www.edelman.com/
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provenance is specified (Edelman) but licensing is marked N/A — users should verify reuse permissions directly with the data owner or hosting platform before redistribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal coverage / dataset versioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Year of dataset creation: 2012. Year of dataset update: 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the dataset's origin and last-update year; users should consider temporal scope when conducting trend analyses or using most recent data.
